method: Human/agent visual inspection of rendered manufacturer PDF pages and retained INAV target sources. These notes do not automatically register or authenticate contracts in the existing digital project.

facts_used: The component-side diagram has USB-C on the right. UART1 pads are labelled T1 and R1 at the lower edge near the DJI connections.
A separate 5V pad is directly above T1, and a G pad is directly above R1. The nearby lower-row 9V pad is not selected for this receiver.
The product page and manual layout label the 5V regulator as 2A; this is a shared rail nameplate, not a measured per-pad current guarantee.
sources.qualification: The illustrated ELRS default uses UART2; the retained HS configuration assigns UART1 to the receiver and UART2 to GPS. No firmware allocation was changed. Physical board matching, voltage tolerances and total shared-rail demand are unresolved.

facts_used: The TOP drawing has U.FL upper left and LED upper right; its lower pads run RX, TX, 5V, G from left to right.
The manual specifies nominal 5V input and CRSF.
sources.qualification: The drawing labels its PCB RP1 V1.2, while the selected product is sold as RP1 V2. Physical revision matching, receiver maximum current, logic levels and input-voltage tolerance are unconfirmed. Nominal 5V was not converted into a guaranteed operating range.

sources.purpose: Existing RX UART1 / GPS UART2 allocation and TX-to-RX crossing.
Retained upstream INAV hardware target; no new firmware image, build or flashing.

wire_length_basis: Provisional design allowance, not CAD-routed or measured.
